comment: One row for each rule of part 1 of the leak rule of D17.20 for the locals of an owning
aggregate type (D17.7): the obligation of each exit kind and its exceptions, the facts of the
owners below the local and the walk that tests them, the verdict, its count and its error, and
the limit of the aggregate work (src/fort/owner/prover.ft). Then the error of each exit that the
pass does not prove, the name of its owner and the note of the limit
(src/fort/owner/report.ft). The first stage runs the cases over FIR text and over lowered fort
source, the work limit and the errors (test/fort/owner/prover_aggregate_test.ft). The second
runs the driver test, which holds the error in each mode. The third runs the oracle test, which
prints a false accept of the owning aggregate locals for each row that makes the pass prove an
exit that a run leaks at, or that drops the error of such an exit. The table runs in the Linux
VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose
The first two rounds of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first two rows are
ones that a full run caught.

stages.name: the aggregate module test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/prover_aggregate_test

stages.name: the driver test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_test

stages.name: the oracle test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/oracle_test
